questions.subtopic: Simple Present Assertive Conversion
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Kailash said, "I maintain the digital evidence storage."

options.text: Kailash said that he maintained the digital evidence storage.
Kailash told that he maintained the digital evidence storage.
Kailash said that he maintains the digital evidence storage.
Kailash said that I maintained the digital evidence storage.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke karan Simple Present 'maintain' Simple Past 'maintained' mein backshift hoga. 1st person pronoun 'I' speaker Kailash ke anusaar 'he' banega. Conjunction 'that' aayega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (C) mein tense backshift missing hai. Option (D) mein 'I' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01 & RC-06: Assertive Conversion & Simple Present Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Reporting Verb Said to ➔ Told & 2nd Person Pronoun
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Anurag said to Priya, "You handle the bail applications efficiently."

options.text: Anurag told to Priya that she handled the bail applications efficiently.
Anurag told Priya that she handled the bail applications efficiently.
Anurag said Priya that she handled the bail applications efficiently.
Anurag told Priya that you handled the bail applications efficiently.

questions.explanation: 'Said to Priya' convert hokar 'told Priya' banega (bina 'to' ke). 2nd person 'You' listener Priya (female singular) ke anusaar 'she' banega. Simple Present 'handle' Simple Past 'handled' mein backshift hoga. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'told to' distractor hai. Option (C) mein 'said Priya' invalid syntax hai. Option (D) mein 'you' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & RC-04: Said to ➔ Told & 2nd Person Shift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Continuous Backshift & Time Shift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The senior clerk said, "The committee members are reviewing the draft now."

options.text: The senior clerk said that the committee members were reviewing the draft then.
The senior clerk said that the committee members are reviewing the draft now.
The senior clerk told that the committee members were reviewing the draft then.
The senior clerk said that the committee members had been reviewing the draft now.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'said' past tense mein hai. Present Continuous 'are reviewing' plural subject 'members' ke anusaar Past Continuous 'were reviewing' banega. Time adverbial 'now' shift hokar 'then' banega. Option (A) dono adjustments accurately execute karta hai. Option (B) mein backshift nahi hua. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) mein 'now' ko retain rakha gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & RC-10: Present Continuous ➔ Past Continuous & Now ➔ Then.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Perfect Backshift with Possessive Adjective Shift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Meera said, "I have submitted my verified credentials."

options.text: Meera said that she has submitted her verified credentials.
Meera said that she had submitted her verified credentials.
Meera told that she had submitted my verified credentials.
Meera said that I had submitted my verified credentials.

questions.explanation: Reporting subject Meera (female singular) hai, isliye 1st person pronouns 'I' ➔ 'she' aur 'my' ➔ 'her' banenge. Present Perfect 'have submitted' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had submitted' banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift missing hai. Option (C) mein 'my' ko change nahi kiya gaya aur 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) mein 'I' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-06: 1st Person Shift & Present Perfect ➔ Past Perfect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Simple Past to Past Perfect Shift & Yesterday Adjustment
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The system admin said, "The server crashed yesterday."

options.text: The system admin said that the server had crashed the previous day.
The system admin said that the server crashed yesterday.
The system admin said that the server crashed the previous day.
The system admin told that the server had crashed yesterday.

questions.explanation: Simple Past 'crashed' past reporting verb ke under Past Perfect 'had crashed' mein backshift hoga. Time expression 'yesterday' convert hokar 'the previous day' banega. Option (A) dono checks satisfy karta hai. Option (B) mein na tense badla na time. Option (C) mein Simple Past ko Simple Past hi chhod diya gaya (classic distractor). Option (D) mein 'yesterday' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07 & RC-10: Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect & Yesterday ➔ The previous day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Past Continuous to Past Perfect Continuous Shift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Vikram said, "We were analyzing the cyber forensic log files."

options.text: Vikram said that they were analyzing the cyber forensic log files.
Vikram said that we had been analyzing the cyber forensic log files.
Vikram said that they had been analyzing the cyber forensic log files.
Vikram told that they had analyzed the cyber forensic log files.

questions.explanation: 1st person plural 'We' Vikram aur uske colleagues ke anusaar 'they' banega. Past Continuous 'were analyzing' past reporting verb ke karan Past Perfect Continuous 'had been analyzing' mein backshift hoga. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift missing hai. Option (B) mein 'we' ko change nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein continuous aspect ko drop karke simple Past Perfect bana diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-07: We ➔ They & Past Continuous ➔ Past Perfect Continuous.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Modal Backshift 'Will' to 'Would'
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The High Court bench said, "The final verdict will be pronounced shortly."

options.text: The High Court bench said that the final verdict will be pronounced shortly.
The High Court bench said that the final verdict would be pronounced shortly.
The High Court bench told that the final verdict would be pronounced shortly.
The High Court bench said that the final verdict should be pronounced shortly.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke karan modal auxiliary 'will' backshift hokar 'would' banegi. Main passive verb chain 'be pronounced' base form mein uninflected rahegi. Option (B) bilkul correct hai. Option (A) mein 'will' ko backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein 'told' bina listener object ke use hua hai. Option (D) mein 'should' (advice) lagakar meaning distort kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Will ➔ Would backshift with past reporting verb.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Modal Backshift 'Can' to 'Could' & Plural Demonstrative Shift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The officer said to the staff, "You cannot bypass these security protocols."

options.text: The officer told to the staff that they could not bypass those security protocols.
The officer told the staff that they could not bypass those security protocols.
The officer told the staff that they cannot bypass these security protocols.
The officer said the staff that they could not bypass those security protocols.

questions.explanation: 'Said to the staff' ➔ 'told the staff'. 2nd person plural 'You' listener 'the staff' ke anusaar 'they' banega. Modal 'cannot' ➔ 'could not' mein badlega. Demonstrative 'these' ➔ 'those' mein shift hoga. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein 'told to' blunder hai. Option (C) mein modal aur demonstrative shift missing hain. Option (D) mein 'said the staff' invalid construction hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02, RC-08 & RC-10: Said to ➔ Told, Can ➔ Could, These ➔ Those.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Modal Backshift 'May' to 'Might'
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The advocate said, "The appellate bench may grant interim stay today."

options.text: The advocate said that the appellate bench might grant interim stay that day.
The advocate said that the appellate bench may grant interim stay today.
The advocate said that the appellate bench might grant interim stay today.
The advocate told that the appellate bench may grant interim stay that day.

questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' ke karan modal 'may' ➔ 'might' mein backshift hoga. Time expression 'today' shift hokar 'that day' banega. Option (A) dono conditions accurately satisfy karta hai. Option (B) mein koi change nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein 'today' ko change nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'told' bina object ke hai aur 'may' ko change nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: May ➔ Might & Today ➔ That day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Modal 'Must' (Past Specific Obligation) ➔ 'Had to'
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Mohit said, "I must submit the compliance affidavit by 4 PM today."

options.text: Mohit said that he must submit the compliance affidavit by 4 PM today.
Mohit said that he had to submit the compliance affidavit by 4 PM that day.
Mohit told that he had to submit the compliance affidavit by 4 PM that day.
Mohit said that he has to submit the compliance affidavit by 4 PM today.

questions.explanation: Specific deadline/obligation express karne wala modal 'must' past reporting verb ke under 'had to' mein badalta hai. 1st person 'I' Mohit ke anusaar 'he' banega aur 'today' ➔ 'that day' banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'must' aur 'today' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya. Option (C) mein 'told' bina listener object ke use kiya gaya hai. Option (D) mein 'has to' present tense laga diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: Must (obligation) ➔ Had to & Today ➔ That day.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Invariance of Already-Past Modals (Should / Could / Would)
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The senior counsel said, "You should thoroughly cross-examine this witness."

options.text: The senior counsel said that I should thoroughly cross-examine that witness.
The senior counsel said that I would thoroughly cross-examine that witness.
The senior counsel told that I had to thoroughly cross-examine this witness.
The senior counsel said that I ought to thoroughly cross-examine that witness.

questions.explanation: Already-past modal 'should' ka koi further past form nahi hota, isliye 'should' uninflected rehta hai. 2nd person 'You' implied listener 'me' ke anusaar 'I' banega aur demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' banega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein 'should' ko 'would' bana diya gaya jo advice ki modality ko distort karta hai. Option (C) mein 'had to' aur 'this' ka distractor hai. Option (D) mein unnecessary modal replacement kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08 & RC-10: Should / Could / Would Invariance & This ➔ That.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Universal Truth Exception: Solar System Fact
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The school principal said, "The Sun rises in the east."

options.text: The school principal said that the Sun rose in the east.
The school principal said that the Sun rises in the east.
The school principal told that the Sun rises in the east.
The school principal said that the Sun has risen in the east.

questions.explanation: 'The Sun rises in the east' ek universal eternal truth hai. Reporting verb past ('said') hone ke bawajood universal truths aur scientific facts ka tense backshift nahi hota; Simple Present 'rises' uninflected rehta hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'rose' likhne se ye imply hota hai ki Suraj ab poorv se nahi nikalta, jo absurd error hai. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) mein Present Perfect distractor hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Universal Truth Exception (Simple Present Retained).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Scientific Fact Exception: Thermal Expansion
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The science professor said, "Metals expand when heated."

options.text: The science professor said that metals expanded when heated.
The science professor said that metals expand when heated.
The science professor told that metals had expanded when heated.
The science professor said that metals would expand when heated.

questions.explanation: 'Metals expand when heated' ek established scientific law hai jo hamesha valid rehta hai. Isliye reporting verb past hone ke bawajood verb 'expand' Simple Present mein hi retain rahegi. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein past tense 'expanded' laga diya gaya jo scientific law ko historical event bana deta hai. Option (C) aur (D) galat modal/aspect distortion karte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Scientific Law Exception to Tense Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Proverbs & Moral Truths Exception
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The venerable judge said, "Honesty is the bedrock of justice."

options.text: The venerable judge said that honesty was the bedrock of justice.
The venerable judge said that honesty is the bedrock of justice.
The venerable judge told that honesty is the bedrock of justice.
The venerable judge said that honesty had been the bedrock of justice.

questions.explanation: Moral maxims, proverbs, aur philosophical truths past reporting verb ke sath bhi Simple Present tense mein retain rehte hain, kyunki unki validity time-bound nahi hoti. Auxiliary 'is' freeze rahegi; 'was' lagane se arth nikalta hai ki honesty pehle bedrock thi par ab nahi hai. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) over-backshifting blunder hai. Option (C) mein 'told' bina object ke hai. Option (D) Past Perfect distractor hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Proverbs & Moral Maxims Invariance.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Present Reporting Verb ('Says') — No Backshift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The chief system architect says, "The cloud network requires multi-factor authentication."

options.text: The chief system architect says that the cloud network required multi-factor authentication.
The chief system architect says that the cloud network requires multi-factor authentication.
The chief system architect said that the cloud network required multi-factor authentication.
The chief system architect told that the cloud network requires multi-factor authentication.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'says' Simple Present Tense mein hai. Narration ka core fundamental rule hai ki jab reporting verb Present ya Future tense mein hoti hai, toh reported speech ke tense mein koi backshift NAHI hota! Verb 'requires' Simple Present mein hi rahegi. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein over-backshift kiya gaya. Option (C) mein reporting verb ko hi past bana diya gaya. Option (D) mein 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Present Reporting Verb ➔ Zero Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Future Reporting Verb ('Will say') — No Backshift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The registrar will say, "The recruitment process is completely transparent."

options.text: The registrar will say that the recruitment process was completely transparent.
The registrar will say that the recruitment process is completely transparent.
The registrar would say that the recruitment process was completely transparent.
The registrar will tell that the recruitment process is completely transparent.

questions.explanation: Reporting verb 'will say' Future Tense mein hai. Jab reporting verb future mein ho, toh reported speech ka tense freeze rehta hai. Auxiliary 'is' uninflected Simple Present mein retain rahegi. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein tense backshift kiya gaya jo future reporting verb ke rule ke against hai. Option (C) mein reporting verb aur reported verb dono ko distort kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'will tell' bina listener object ke use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Future Reporting Verb ➔ Zero Backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Compound Sentence Multi-Clause Backshift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
Kunal said to Ritu, "I completed the data entry, but the database connection was unstable."

options.text: Kunal told Ritu that he completed the data entry, but the database connection was unstable.
Kunal told Ritu that he had completed the data entry, but the database connection had been unstable.
Kunal told to Ritu that he had completed the data entry, but the database connection had been unstable.
Kunal told Ritu that he had completed the data entry, but the database connection was unstable.

questions.explanation: 'Said to Ritu' ➔ 'told Ritu'. 1st person 'I' Kunal ke anusaar 'he' banega. Sentence compound hai jisme do past coordinate clauses hain: (1) Simple Past 'completed' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had completed' banega, aur (2) Simple Past 'was unstable' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had been unstable' banega. Option (B) dono clauses mein consistent aur harmonious backshift execute karta hai. Option (A) mein backshift nahi hua. Option (C) mein 'told to' blunder hai. Option (D) mein coordinate clause ka backshift incomplete chhod diya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & RC-07: Compound Multi-Clause Backshift Coordination.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Temporal & Locational Adverbial Multi-Shift
questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech for the sentence:
The assistant said, "I placed the sealed evidence box here two days ago."

options.text: The assistant said that he placed the sealed evidence box there two days ago.
The assistant said that he had placed the sealed evidence box there two days before.
The assistant said that he had placed the sealed evidence box here two days before.
The assistant told that he has placed the sealed evidence box there two days ago.

questions.explanation: Is sentence mein 3 mandatory shifts hain: (1) Simple Past 'placed' ➔ Past Perfect 'had placed', (2) Place adverb 'here' ➔ 'there', aur (3) Time adverb 'two days ago' ➔ 'two days before'. Option (B) in teeno rules ko flawlessly apply karta hai. Option (A) mein tense aur 'ago' ko backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein 'here' ko unadjusted chhod diya gaya. Option (D) mein 'has placed' aur 'told' bina object ke hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07 & RC-10: Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect, Here ➔ There, Ago ➔ Before.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Spotting the Only Flawless Indirect Construction
questions.question:
Select the only grammatically flawless Indirect Speech transformation:
Direct: Geeta said to Mahesh, "I will return your legal commentary book tomorrow."

options.text: Geeta told to Mahesh that she would return his legal commentary book the following day.
Geeta told Mahesh that she will return his legal commentary book tomorrow.
Geeta told Mahesh that she would return his legal commentary book the following day.
Geeta told Mahesh that he would return her legal commentary book the next day.

questions.explanation: Step-by-step evaluation: (1) 'Said to Mahesh' ➔ 'told Mahesh' (no 'to'), (2) 'I' ➔ 'she' (Geeta), (3) 'your' ➔ 'his' (Mahesh), (4) 'will' ➔ 'would', aur (5) 'tomorrow' ➔ 'the following day' (ya 'the next day'). Option (C) in sabhi 5 checkpoints par 100% accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'told to Mahesh' fatal error hai. Option (B) mein 'will' aur 'tomorrow' unmodified hain. Option (D) mein pronouns interchange kar diye gaye ('he would return her book' se meaning ulta ho gaya).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02, RC-03, RC-04, RC-08 & RC-10: Master 5-Step Synthesis.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting in Complex Reported Speech
questions.question: Which of the following indirect speech sentences contains a grammatical error?

options.text: The bench declared that the constitutional amendment was valid.
The geography professor explained that the Amazon river flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
The IT consultant told to the director that the server had been compromised.
The court clerk stated that the daily cause list had been uploaded on the portal.

questions.explanation: Sentence (C) mein grammatical error hai kyunki yahan 'told to the director' likha gaya hai. 'Tell' transitive verb hone ke karan preposition 'to' nahi leti; correct form 'told the director' honi chahiye. Sentences (A), (B), aur (D) bilkul correct hain: (A) mein Simple Past backshift accurate hai, (B) mein permanent geographical fact hone ke karan 'flows' Simple Present mein retain hai (valid exception), aur (D) mein 'stated that' past perfect passive ke sath bilkul flawless hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & Pitfall PIT-01: 'Told to + Object' Prepositional Blunder.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L06
